sources.title: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale
sources.reading_scope: Complete original AMD October 12 release, reference OCP design, configurable cooling, EPYC-only versus EPYC+Instinct MI350P racks, token routing, partner comments, actual planned November availability and forward-looking caveats.
factual_findings: Helion is an open agentic computing rack blueprint rather than a verified shipped rack.
CPU-only reference configuration includes up to 32,768 sixth-generation EPYC cores.
Combined enterprise design pairs EPYC CPU and MI350P GPU nodes.
AMD plans OCP contribution and partner availability in November 2026, not general availability today.

sources.title: One Agent Development Kit, five languages
sources.reading_scope: Entire developer article, the MCP/A2A shared interoperability architecture and original per-language examples across Python signature inference, Go struct/generics graph workflows, TypeScript Zod, Java schema annotations, Kotlin compile-time KSP and evaluation.
factual_findings: Five native ADK runtimes are Python, Go, TypeScript, Java and Kotlin.
All five speak MCP for tools and A2A for cross-agent communications.
Different runtimes infer and validate tool input schemas differently.
Google cites Python golden trajectory eval, Go graph workflow and zero reflection Kotlin code generation.

sources.title: 83% of Agent Skills have no license
sources.reading_scope: Full dated SkillMD October 10 sample/results, methodology, example frontmatter, SPDX advice, linter SK011, duplicate normalization and limitations regarding repo-level licenses.
factual_findings: Registry measured 1,081,266 public indexed SKILL.md files; 901,653 have no license frontmatter field, 83.4%.
Survey DID NOT check repository-level LICENSE, so lack of frontmatter is not proof of absent project license.
Free-text terms differ even when legally equivalent; SPDX standardization needed.
Build a reusable read-only provenance and license review Agent Skill; never execute unknown skill before manual approval.
sources.freshness_reason: October 10 dated first-party methodology within 168 hours fills practical Agent Skills review gap that newer launch articles do not; explicitly limits inferred licensing conclusions.

read_evidence.scope: Full dated SkillMD October 10 sample/results, methodology, example frontmatter, SPDX advice, linter SK011, duplicate normalization and limitations regarding repo-level licenses.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon comes to the Gemini app
sources.reading_scope: Complete Google October 13 Gemini app release covering task versus chat toggle, connected third-party apps, macOS coding pathway, Pro/Ultra eligibility and task progress updates.
factual_findings: Google reports a main-chat toggle lets users choose task-oriented agent execution.
It reports 40-plus connected applications including Instacart, OpenTable, Adobe and Shopify.
Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can access Argon and assign Gemini tasks.
No cited independent measurements of task accuracy or authorization guarantees; recommend bounded review.
